parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
B1 From $2x=\tan\theta$, obtain $x=\frac12\tan\theta$ and $dx=\frac12\sec^2\theta\,d\theta$. Guidance: May be stated or implied by a correct substitution line.
B1 Change limits: $x=0\Rightarrow\theta=0$ and $x=\frac12\Rightarrow\theta=\frac\pi4$. Guidance: Both transformed limits required.
B1 Use $1+4x^2=1+\tan^2\theta=\sec^2\theta$. Guidance: Accept equivalent within the transformed integral.
M1 Substitute consistently to obtain $\int_0^{\pi/4}\frac{12}{\sec^4\theta}(\frac12\sec^2\theta)\,d\theta$, or equivalent.
A1 Obtain $6\int_0^{\pi/4}\cos^2\theta\,d\theta$.
M1 Use $\cos^2\theta=\frac12(1+\cos2\theta)$, or another correct method for integrating $\cos^2\theta$.
A1 Obtain $[3\theta+\frac32\sin2\theta]_0^{\pi/4}$, or an exact equivalent antiderivative.
M1 Use the transformed limits correctly in a correct trigonometric antiderivative.
A1 Obtain $\frac{3\pi}{4}+\frac32$. Guidance: Exact answer required; accept terms reversed or exact algebraic equivalent.
Total: 9 marks.
Provenance notice: supervisor-authorized generated substitute; NOT Cambridge official.
